items.q: Can my child try a class first?
items.a: Yes. Any student can sit in on two classes before paying, after the placement test.

items.q: What if my child misses a class?
items.a: Notes are kept at the desk, and the teacher goes through the missed topic in the doubt-clearing hour on Saturday morning.

items.q: How will I know how my child is doing?
items.a: Friday test marks and attendance are sent on Viber at the end of every month. You can ask to meet any teacher on Saturday.
Students from community schools with a GPA of 3.6 or more in Class 9 pay half fees for SEE preparation. Bring the mark sheet.

items.q: Are girls and boys taught together?
items.a: Yes, in all batches. There is a woman staff member at the desk from 6:00 to 19:00.

pages.title: Bridge course
pages.seoTitle: Bridge course after SEE in Kathmandu · Ujyalo Learning Centre
pages.seoDescription: Eight weeks of Maths, Science and English after SEE, with two model entrance tests and college advice. Rs 9,500, Putalisadak.

props.title: The bridge course, for students waiting on SEE results
props.text: Eight weeks that turn three idle months into a head start in +2 Science, and prepare students for college entrance tests.

image.alt: A teacher talking to a small class seated at long desks

props.eyebrow: Starts the week after SEE ends · Rs 9,500

props.heading: Why a bridge course
props.body:
Class 11 Science moves fast. Students who arrive already comfortable with vectors, the mole and the cell keep up; the rest spend the first term catching up.

Most good +2 colleges also hold an entrance test in Jestha. The bridge course ends with two full model tests in the same format, and a one-to-one talk about which colleges suit which student.

props.heading: How we teach
props.body:
Every class starts with five minutes on last class’s homework. Every chapter ends with a short test. Every Friday, a longer one.

Teachers mark their own papers. It takes longer, but it means the person who taught the chapter sees the mistakes and can fix them on Sunday.

  • Twenty students to a batch, at most
  • A doubt-clearing hour on Saturday, 8:00 to 9:00
  • Old board and entrance papers for every chapter
